'''Alfred Ngaro''' is a New Zealand politician, who served as leader of [[NewZeal]] from 2023 to 2026. 
He was a list member of the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]] from [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011]] to [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]], representing the [[New Zealand National Party|National Party]].

Ngaro is the first New Zealander of [[Cook Islands]] descent to be elected to Parliament in New Zealand. He was [[Minister for Pacific Peoples]] and [[Minister for the Community and Voluntary Sector]] in the final year of the [[Fifth National Government of New Zealand]].

He was later elected leader of the socially conservative New Zeal party in July 2023, and unsuccessfully stood as a list candidate at the [[2023 New Zealand general election|subsequent general election]]. In March 2026 Ngaro was introduced as a [[New Zealand First]] candidate for the [[2026 New Zealand general election]].<ref name="NZH 22 Mar 2026">{{cite news |last1=Pearse |first1=Adam |date=22 March 2026 |title=Winston Peters' State of the Nation: Former National minister Alfred Ngaro to stand for NZ First|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/winston-peters-state-of-the-nation-new-candidate-and-energy-policy-expected-in-tauranga-address/FCZ3PZ23HRELDBZV5CC2RCVRS4/|access-date=22 March 2026 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260322221828/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/winston-peters-state-of-the-nation-new-candidate-and-energy-policy-expected-in-tauranga-address/FCZ3PZ23HRELDBZV5CC2RCVRS4/ |archive-date=22 March 2026|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Early life==
Ngaro was raised in [[Te Atatū South|Te Atatū]] and attended the local schools of Edmonton Primary, [[Rangeview Intermediate School|Rangeview Intermediate]] and [[Henderson High School, Auckland|Henderson High School]].<ref name="Ngaro bio">{{Cite web|url=https://alfredngaro.national.org.nz/about_alfred|title=About Alfred|website=Hon Alfred Ngaro|language=en|access-date=2019-08-17|archive-date=17 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190817060202/https://alfredngaro.national.org.nz/about_alfred|url-status=dead}} [[File:CC BY-SA icon.svg|50px]] This article contains quotations from this source, which is available under the [https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/nz/ Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 New Zealand (CC BY 3.0 New Zealand)] license.</ref> Both his parents came from the [[Cook Islands]].<ref name=Address_in_Reply>{{cite web |url= https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/50HansS_20111221_00000161/ngaro-alfred-address-in-reply |title=Ngaro, Alfred: Address in Reply |first=Ngaro |last=Alfred |date=21 December 2011 |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |access-date=6 August 2019}}</ref> Ngaro's father, Daniel Ngaro, is from [[Aitutaki]]<ref name="Inspiring Communities bio">{{cite web|title=Alfred Ngaro|url=http://www.inspiringcommunities.org.nz/about-us/147-alfred-ngaro|publisher=Inspiring Communities|access-date=5 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100601225347/http://www.inspiringcommunities.org.nz/about-us/147-alfred-ngaro|archive-date=1 June 2010|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and [[Pukapuka]], and was a union delegate. The family have a long tradition of voting for the [[New Zealand Labour Party|Labour Party]].<ref name=tradition>{{cite news |last=Romanos |first=Amelia|title='Cook Island Kiwi' breaks with tradition |url= http://www.nzherald.co.nz/cook-islanders-in-nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1500949&objectid=10763529 |access-date=5 December 2011|work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=3 November 2011}}</ref> His mother, Toko Kirianu, is from [[Mangaia]].<ref name="Inspiring Communities bio" /> His parents worked hard, his mother as a cleaner and his father as a labourer, to give Ngaro and his siblings education and training opportunities.<ref name="Syme-Buchanan">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cookislandsnews.com/item/62187-first-cook-islander-in-nz-cabinet/62187-first-cook-islander-in-nz-cabinet|title=First Cook Islander in NZ Cabinet|last=Syme-Buchanan|first=Florence|website=www.cookislandsnews.com|language=en-gb|access-date=2019-08-17}}</ref>

Ngaro's grandmother, Rita Goldstein, is of both Cook Island and [[Jews|Jewish]] descent, her father being of [[Polish-Jewish]] ancestry.<ref name="Israel Institute" /><ref name="AIJAC" /><ref name="One Community Chronicle" /> Ngaro has described himself as "Polynesian by birth and Jewish by descent".<ref name="One Community Chronicle" /> His wife Mokauina is of Samoan-Niuean descent.<ref name="tradition" /><ref name="Radio Australia">{{cite news |date=28 November 2011 |title=New National Party Pacific MP in NZ |url=http://www.radioaustralia.net.au/pacbeat/stories/201111/s3378462.htm |access-date=5 December 2011 |work=Radio Australia}}</ref> They have four children: three boys and one girl.<ref name="Inspiring Communities bio" /><ref name="Radio Australia" />

He trained and qualified as an electrician and also completed his theological degree at the Henderson campus of the Bible College of New Zealand (now [[Laidlaw College]]). Prior to entering Parliament, Ngaro was a consultant in community-led development and governance with expertise in New Zealand, Cook Islands and Canada. He co-pioneered several community initiatives such as the Tamaki Achievement Pathway, Healthy Village Action Zone (HVAZ) Project, and the Inspiring Communities Exchange Network sponsored by the [[Tindall Foundation]].<ref name="Ngaro bio"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pacific.scoop.co.nz/2014/06/national-selects-alfred-ngaro-as-te-atatu-candidate/|title=Pacific.scoop.co.nz » National selects Alfred Ngaro as Te Atatu candidate|language=en|access-date=2019-08-17}}</ref> Ngaro's governance experience includes key roles on the National Family Violence Taskforce, [[Auckland District Health Board]] and Pacific Advisory Committee [[Auckland City Council]]. He is also an Ambassador for the [[White Ribbon campaign]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://tvnz.co.nz/raising-children-in-new-zealand/alfred-ngaro-4170205|title=Raising Children in New Zealand}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://whiteribbon.org.nz/act/ambassadors/|title=Ambassadors|date=2010-08-27|website=White Ribbon New Zealand|language=en-US|access-date=2019-08-17}}</ref><ref name="Syme-Buchanan"/> He later won a Sir Peter Blake Emerging Leader Award for his work on the Tamaki Transformation Project.<ref name="Ngaro bio"/><ref name="Inspiring Communities Blake Leadership award">{{cite web|title=Alfred Ngaro wins Sir Peter Blake Leadership award|url=http://www.inspiringcommunities.org.nz/community-news/201-alfred-ngaro-wins-sir-peter-blake-leadership-award|publisher=Inspiring Communities|access-date=5 December 2011|date=29 June 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426021455/http://www.inspiringcommunities.org.nz/community-news/201-alfred-ngaro-wins-sir-peter-blake-leadership-award|archive-date=26 April 2012|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

==Early political career==
Ngaro served as the [[Auckland District Health Board]]'s Pacific committee chairman and as the Tamaki College board of trustees chairman.<ref name=tradition/> He was a member of various advisory committees for the [[Ministry of Social Development (New Zealand)|Ministry of Social Development]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Alfred Ngaro|url=http://www.raisingchildren.org.nz/2011/05/alfred-ngaro/|publisher=Raising Children in New Zealand|access-date=5 December 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426021741/http://www.raisingchildren.org.nz/2011/05/alfred-ngaro/|archive-date=26 April 2012|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Ngaro was encouraged by his friend [[Sam Lotu-Iiga]], then the first-term National MP in [[Maungakiekie (New Zealand electorate)|Maungakiekie]] and a former Auckland City Councillor in Maungakiekie, to become active in politics.<ref name="tradition" /> Ngaro contested the new [[Maungakiekie-Tāmaki ward]] on the [[Auckland Council]] at the [[2010 Auckland local elections]], as a [[Citizens and Ratepayers]] candidate. His campaign manager was [[Denise Lee|Denise Krum]].<ref>{{cite news |date=13 October 2010 |title=Alfred Ngaro valiant in defeat |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1010/S00136/alfred-ngaro-valiant-in-defeat.htm |access-date=5 December 2011 |work=Scoop}}</ref> Ngaro finished second to [[Richard Northey]] and was not elected.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Pamatatau |first=Richard |date=2017-05-20 |title=Richard Pamatatau: Alfred Ngaro has soured his brand |url=https://e-tangata.co.nz/comment-and-analysis/richard-pamatatau-alfred-ngaro-has-soured-his-brand/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=E-Tangata |language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cooke |first=Michelle |date=1 October 2010 |title=Tight race for council seat |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/4182499/Tight-race-for-council-seat |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McGillivray |first=Amy |date=13 October 2010 |title=Northey wins in tough contest |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/east-bays-courier/4223397/Northey-wins-in-tough-contest |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref> He reportedly said, in his concession statement on election night, that "'the sandpit of local government' was not for him and he would aim higher to where the 'big people' play."<ref name=":0" />

In early September 2011, Ngaro was announced as a list-only candidate for the [[New Zealand National Party]] at the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 election]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Goodfellow|first=Peter|title=New Faces In National's 2011 Party List|url=http://www.national.org.nz/Article.aspx?articleId=36979|publisher=National Party|access-date=5 December 2011|date=4 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111018172052/http://www.national.org.nz/Article.aspx?ArticleID=36979|archive-date=18 October 2011|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He was ranked 37th on the party list<ref name="electionsnz-final">{{cite web|url=http://www.elections.org.nz/elections/2011-general-election-and-referendum/party-lists.html |title=Party lists for the 2011 General Election |publisher=Elections New Zealand |access-date=14 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204010618/http://www.elections.org.nz/elections/2011-general-election-and-referendum/party-lists.html |archive-date=4 February 2012 }}</ref> and was subsequently elected to the [[50th New Zealand Parliament|50th Parliament]].<ref name="25 new MPs">{{cite news|title=Twenty-five new faces for Parliament|url=http://www.3news.co.nz/Twenty-five-new-faces-for-Parliament/tabid/419/articleID/234303/Default.aspx|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130222215755/http://www.3news.co.nz/Twenty-five-new-faces-for-Parliament/tabid/419/articleID/234303/Default.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=22 February 2013|access-date=5 December 2011|work=3 News|date=27 November 2011}}</ref><ref name="2011 successful candidates">{{cite web|title=Official Count Results – Successful Candidates |url= http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2011/successfulcand.html |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission|access-date=13 December 2011}}</ref> He is the first Cook Islander to be elected to the New Zealand Parliament.<ref>{{cite news|title=Key Talks Up Nz Election Policies On Pasifika Issues|url= http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/WO1111/S00604/key-talks-up-nz-election-policies-on-pasifika-issues.htm |access-date=5 December 2011 |work=Scoop|date=21 November 2011}}</ref> In the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]], Ngaro was the National Party candidate for {{NZ electorate link|Te Atatū}}. He lost to Labour's [[Phil Twyford]] by 2,813 votes. Ranked 34th on the National Party list, Ngaro returned to parliament for his second term as a National list MP.

Between 2011 and 2016, during the second and third terms of the [[Fifth National Government of New Zealand|Fifth National Government]], Ngaro was a member of the justice and electoral committee and the social services committee. He was deputy chair of the justice and electoral committee in 2013, deputy chair of the social services committee in 2014, and chair of the social services committee after the [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 general election]] until his promotion into the ministry.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Ngaro, Alfred - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/former-members-of-parliament/ngaro-alfred/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref>

Ngaro was the member in charge of the Local Government (Auckland Council) Amendment Bill (No 3).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Local Government (Auckland Council) Amendment Bill (No 3) |url=https://bills.parliament.nz/v/6/bcadefbd-e78c-4eeb-8373-4ebb61a0db2e |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=bills.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> This bill proposed amendments to the legislation governing [[Auckland Council]] that would prohibit candidates from holding office in more than one [[Local boards of Auckland Council|local board]] area. The bill was informally known as the "Warren Flaunty bill" after a pharmacist and politician who was elected to three local boards in the [[2010 Auckland local elections|2010 Auckland elections]] and two local boards in the [[2013 Auckland local elections|2013 Auckland elections]]. The bill passed into law in May 2016 with the support of National and Labour, and was implemented ahead of the [[2016 New Zealand local elections|2016 local elections]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Simon |date=2016-05-19 |title='Warren Flaunty Bill' stops politicians sitting on multiple Auckland local boards |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/80139668/warren-flaunty-bill-stops-politicians-sitting-on-multiple-auckland-local-boards |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref>

Ngaro, during his time as a backbench member of Parliament, was described as "one of Parliament's nice guys"<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-15 |title=It's a third-term thing - why Alfred Ngaro hurt National |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/92609745/its-a-third-term-thing--why-alfred-ngaro-hurt-national |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref> and "a compliant party servant with a clear elevation strategy and part of a Pacific double act alongside [[Sam Lotu-Iiga|Peseta [Sam Lotu-Iiga]]]."<ref name=":0" /> He was instrumental in getting Cook Islands World War One soldiers formally recognised by the New Zealand government for their role during the [[World War I|Great War]].<ref name="Syme-Buchanan" /> During the [[2016 New Zealand National Party leadership election]], Ngaro was identified as part of an internal party grouping of influential backbenchers nicknamed the "Four Amigos" with [[Chris Bishop]], [[Todd Muller]] and [[Mark Mitchell (New Zealand politician)|Mark Mitchell]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Backbenchers 'Four Amigos' key to future National leader's success |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2016/12/backbenchers-four-amigos-key-to-future-national-leaders-success.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201028235804/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2016/12/backbenchers-four-amigos-key-to-future-national-leaders-success.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=28 October 2020 |access-date=2024-01-15 |work=[[Newshub]] |language=en}}</ref> The group had come together campaigning for National in the [[2015 Northland by-election]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moir |first=Jo |date=2016-12-07 |title=How much weight do four National backbenchers hold over who will be the next Prime Minister? |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/opinion/87299607/how-much-weight-do-four-national-backbenchers-hold-over-who-will-be-the-next-prime-minister |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref> After the group put their support behind [[Bill English]], Ngaro was promoted into the Cabinet, earning him the descriptor of the biggest winner in English's first ministerial reshuffle.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Moir |first=Jo |date=2016-12-18 |title=Who are the winners and losers in Bill English's Cabinet reshuffle? |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/87699167/who-are-the-winners-and-losers-in-bill-englishs-cabinet-reshuffle |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en}}</ref>

=== Minister in the Fifth National Government ===
Ngaro was sworn in as [[Minister for Pacific Peoples]], [[Minister for the Community and Voluntary Sector]], Associate Minister for Children and Associate Minister for Social Housing on 20 December 2016.<ref name=":1" />

As minister, Ngaro increased the funding of [[Polyfest]], the world's largest pacific festival.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New funding will allow Polyfest to grow {{!}} Beehive.govt.nz |url=https://beehive.govt.nz/release/new-funding-will-allow-polyfest-grow |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=beehive.govt.nz |language=en}}</ref> He launched a policy analysis framework for promoting Pacific perspectives in government decision-making.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pacific perspective at the forefront with launch of policy tool {{!}} Beehive.govt.nz |url=https://beehive.govt.nz/release/pacific-perspective-forefront-launch-policy-tool |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=beehive.govt.nz |language=en}}</ref> He also led the purchase by the government of motels in [[Gisborne, New Zealand|Gisborne]] and [[Hawke's Bay]] in an attempt to address social housing shortfalls in those regions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former motel coming online to help Gisborne homeless {{!}} Beehive.govt.nz |url=https://beehive.govt.nz/release/former-motel-coming-online-help-gisborne-homeless |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=beehive.govt.nz |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Two former motels coming online to help Hawke's Bay homeless {{!}} Beehive.govt.nz |url=https://beehive.govt.nz/release/two-former-motels-coming-online-help-hawke%E2%80%99s-bay-homeless |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=beehive.govt.nz |language=en}}</ref>

In May 2017, he told a National Party conference that he could cut government funding to organisations associated with Labour candidate [[Willie Jackson (politician)|Willie Jackson]] if Jackson spoke out against the government during the election campaign. He apologised after his words were criticised by both Labour leader [[Andrew Little (New Zealand politician)|Andrew Little]] and Minister of Finance [[Steven Joyce]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=14 May 2017 |title=Ngaro apologises for govt criticism |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/330743/ngaro-apologises-for-govt-criticism}}</ref> Prime Minister Bill English subsequently offered reassurances to community agencies that they would always be free to express views on government policy, and announced that he had asked officials to review the decisions Ngaro had made as a minister. Ngaro did not offer his resignation.<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 May 2017 |title=NGOs 'always free' to speak out about government policy – PM |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/330824/ngos-always-free-to-speak-out-about-government-policy-pm}}</ref>

=== Opposition, 2017–2020 ===
Ngaro unsuccessfully contested [[Te Atatū (New Zealand electorate)|Te Atatū]] for a second time at the [[2017 New Zealand general election|2017 general election]]. The National Government was also defeated. Ngaro became National's spokesperson for children, the community and voluntary sector, and pacific peoples. He sat on the social services and community committee.<ref name=":1" />

In mid-May 2019, there were reports that Ngaro was considering forming his own Christian party, providing a potential coalition partner for National at the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 general election]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Satherley |first1=Dan |title=Alfred Ngaro to set up Christian conservative party – report |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/05/alfred-ngaro-to-set-up-christian-conservative-party-report.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190517051437/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/05/alfred-ngaro-to-set-up-christian-conservative-party-report.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 May 2019 |access-date=29 May 2019 |publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=17 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Soper |first1=Barry |title=National needs friends ... Is former Cabinet Minister Alfred Ngaro the answer? |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12231733 |access-date=29 May 2019 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=17 May 2019}}</ref> National Party leader [[Simon Bridges]] initially downplayed these reports but later stated that he was giving Ngaro the "space" to explore setting up a Christian values party.<ref>{{cite news |title=Breakaway Christian party just 'rumour and speculation' – Bridges |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/389392/breakaway-christian-party-just-rumour-and-speculation-bridges |access-date=29 May 2019 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=17 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Simon Bridges on Botany: 'We will win that seat for National' |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/389578/simon-bridges-on-botany-we-will-win-that-seat-for-national |access-date=29 May 2019 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=20 May 2019}}</ref> In late May 2019, Ngaro ruled out starting a new Christian party and confirmed that he would remain a member of the National Party.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alfred Ngaro decides against forming Christian party |url=https://embed.radionz.co.nz/news/political/390722/alfred-ngaro-decides-against-forming-christian-party |access-date=29 May 2019 |publisher=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=28 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=MP Alfred Ngaro will not split off from National to start new Christian party |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12235050 |access-date=29 May 2019 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=28 May 2019}}</ref> He contested the 2020 general election for National, standing for a third time in Te Atatū and placed at 30th on the party list.

Ngaro attracted media attention during the election campaign when he posted a [[Facebook]] [[attack ad]] claiming that a vote for his Labour opponent [[Phil Twyford]] would lead to the decriminalisation of recreational cannabis and all drugs and unlimited abortion. Though Ngaro subsequently deleted his post, Twyford captured a screenshot and accused his opponent of spreading [[fake news]]. Ngaro's post was also criticised by Labour MP [[Ruth Dyson]], Auckland councillor [[Richard Hills (politician)|Richard Hills]], political commentator Ben Thomas, and former [[Internet Party (New Zealand)|Internet Party]] leader [[Laila Harré]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Satherley |first1=Dan |title=NZ Election 2020: National MP Alfred Ngaro accused of spreading 'gross piece of misinformation' on Facebook |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/10/nz-election-2020-national-mp-alfred-ngaro-accused-of-spreading-gross-piece-of-misinformation-on-facebook.html |access-date=10 October 2020 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=10 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010081248/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/10/nz-election-2020-national-mp-alfred-ngaro-accused-of-spreading-gross-piece-of-misinformation-on-facebook.html |archive-date=10 October 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref> In addition, National Party leader [[Judith Collins]] issued a media statement that Ngaro's comments were not shared by the rest of the party.<ref>{{cite news |title=Collins intervenes after controversial abortion post |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/428028/collins-intervenes-after-controversial-abortion-post |access-date=10 October 2020 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=10 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010081611/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/428028/collins-intervenes-after-controversial-abortion-post |archive-date=10 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Twyford defeated Ngaro by a final margin of 10,508 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Te Atatū - Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-53.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=13 November 2020 }}</ref> Since he did not rank highly enough on the National's party list, he also lost his seat.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Whyte |first1=Anna |title=Analysis: The winners, losers, new faces and goodbyes of election 2020 |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/analysis-winners-losers-new-faces-and-goodbyes-election-2020 |access-date=22 October 2020 |work=[[1News]] |date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022090204/https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/analysis-winners-losers-new-faces-and-goodbyes-election-2020 |archive-date=22 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> Ngaro departed Parliament on 21 October after delivering a dawn prayer and a rendition of the national anthem [[God Defend New Zealand]] on the steps of Parliament.<ref>{{cite news |title=Departing MP Alfred Ngaro delivers prayer on Parliament steps |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/departing-mp-alfred-ngaro-delivers-prayer-on-parliament-steps/3QFUE7LNSP6QMAWEW7KGNIVUEA/ |access-date=22 October 2020 |work=[[New Zealand Herald]] |date=21 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022091732/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/departing-mp-alfred-ngaro-delivers-prayer-on-parliament-steps/3QFUE7LNSP6QMAWEW7KGNIVUEA/ |archive-date=22 October 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Out of Parliament, 2023–present==
=== NewZeal party leadership ===
In 2023, the Christian conservative ONE Party rebranded as [[NewZeal]] and announced Ngaro as their leader.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2023/change-to-party-name-and-logo/ |title=Change to party name and logo |date=16 August 2023 |publisher=Electoral Commission}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/real-life-alfred-ngaro-explains-why-he-turned-his-back-on-national-party-to-launch-new-zeal/5ML6ZNUOAZD4HOF2MC36LOJP34/ |title=Real Life: Alfred Ngaro explains why he turned his back on National Party to launch New Zeal |date=14 August 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |first=Matt |last=Burrows}}</ref> Of his joining NewZeal, Ngaro said: "I haven't moved from my values. I just feel that the National Party has moved away from some of the values that I've upheld."<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-16 |title=Former National Party minister set to launch new Christian party |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/election-2023-former-national-party-minister-alfred-ngaro-set-to-launch-new-christian-party/LA6PRUVYPNBXLOIZVJDCOA55GI/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref> Specifically, Ngaro said National's support of the Labour government's [[Births, Deaths, Marriages, and Relationships Registration Act 2021|enactment of gender self-identification laws in 2021]] and its [[Conversion Practices Prohibition Legislation Act 2022|decision to prohibit conversion therapy]] in 2022 were a departure "from the values I held [and] believed the party was about."<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2024-01-16 |title=Alfred Ngaro explains why he turned his back on National Party to launch New Zeal |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/real-life-alfred-ngaro-explains-why-he-turned-his-back-on-national-party-to-launch-new-zeal/5ML6ZNUOAZD4HOF2MC36LOJP34/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref> He defined himself and the party as [[Centrism|centrist]] but sharing common interests with the centre-right National Party, and refuted that NewZeal was a Christian party.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

During the [[2023 New Zealand general election]] held on 14 October, Ngaro stood as a list-only candidate and led NewZeal to 0.56 percent of the total votes cast (16,126 votes), below the five percent threshold needed to enter Parliament.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 General Election - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/index.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231125022036/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/index.html |archive-date=25 November 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Ngaro subsequently contested the [[2023 Port Waikato by-election]] in late November 2023 as a NewZeal candidate. He came third in a diminished field after the withdrawal of Labour, Green and ACT New Zealand candidates, earning 409 votes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Port Waikato - Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |date=6 December 2023|access-date=7 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207202840/https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2023_port_waikato_byelection/index.html|archive-date=7 December 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

In March 2026, Ngaro resigned as leader of NewZeal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2026 |title=NewZeal Party facebook post |url=https://www.facebook.com/newzealnz/posts/pfbid03YxCaEcHkY8wFuQxa37bdYd8wMLrXtkQFcqDgL8mxCrQPEFUcucASHXXwE6TyExyl?rdid=UHBhdgyiyecwZp7l |access-date=23 March 2026 |website=Facebook}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is insufficiently reliable ([[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=March 2026}}

===New Zealand First candidate===
On 22 March 2026, Ngaro attended [[New Zealand First]] leader [[Winston Peters]]' State of the Nation address in Tauranga where he announced that he would be standing as a candidate for the party during the [[2026 New Zealand general election]].<ref name="NZH 22 Mar 2026" /> That same day, Ngaro confirmed that he and the NewZeal party would align with New Zealand First, citing "strategic realism and shared values."<ref>{{cite web |title=FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE - Alfred Ngaro Announces Alignment with New Zealand First |url=https://newzeal.org.nz/press-releases/for-immediate-release-alfred-ngaro-announces-alignment-with-new-zealand-first |publisher=[[NewZeal]] |access-date=22 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260322221432/https://newzeal.org.nz/press-releases/for-immediate-release-alfred-ngaro-announces-alignment-with-new-zealand-first |archive-date=22 March 2026 |date=22 March 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> 

On 17 May 2026, Ngaro was announced as the party candidate for the [[Glendene_(electorate)|Glendene]] electorate.<ref>{{cite news |title=Winston Peters unveils KiwiSaver-from-birth NZ First policy, bank takeover plan |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/595475/winston-peters-unveils-kiwisaver-from-birth-nz-first-policy-bank-takeover-plan |access-date=17 May 2026 |work=RNZ |date=17 May 2026}}</ref>

==Views and advocacy==
Ngaro is a [[Christianity|Christian]] and a self-described [[Christian Zionism|Christian Zionist]].<ref name="One Community Chronicle">{{cite web|url=https://1.org.nz/mp-alfred-ngaro-declares-his-support-for-israel-and-the-jewish-people/|title=MP Alfred Ngaro declares his support for Israel and the Jewish people|publisher=One Community Chronicle|access-date=9 February 2019}}</ref> Ngaro holds a theology degree and served as a community pastor.<ref name="Israel Institute">{{cite web|url=https://israelinstitute.nz/2018/11/an-mps-call-to-arms/|title=An MP's call to arms|last1=Bell|first1=Miriam|publisher=Israel Institute of New Zealand|access-date=9 February 2019|date=12 November 2018}}</ref><ref name="AIJAC">{{cite web|url=https://aijac.org.au/australia-israel-review/air-new-zealand-an-mps-call-to-arms/|title=AIR New Zealand: An MP's call to arms|last1=Bell|first1=Miriam|publisher=[[AIJAC]]|access-date=9 February 2019|date=8 November 2018}}</ref>

As a member of Parliament, Ngaro voted conservatively on social issues. Ngaro voted against the [[Marriage (Definition of Marriage) Amendment Act 2013|Marriage (Definition of Marriage) Amendment Bill]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=18 April 2013 |title=Gay marriage bill: How MPs voted |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/rotorua-daily-post/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503438&objectid=11096713 |access-date=2 June 2019 |work=Rotorua Post}}</ref> the [[End of Life Choice Act 2019|End of Life Choice Bill]]<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ngaro |first=Alfred |date=21 February 2018 |title=National MP Alfred Ngaro plans to vote against euthanasia |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/auckland/local-news/western-leader/101543666/national-mp-alfred-ngaro-plans-to-vote-against-euthanasia |access-date=2019-08-16 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1905/S00379/the-nation-national-list-mp-alfred-ngaro.htm |title=The Nation: National list MP Alfred Ngaro |date=25 May 2019 |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |publisher=[[Newshub#Newshub Nation|Newshub Nation]] |access-date=2019-08-16}}</ref> and the [[Abortion Legislation Act 2020|Abortion Legislation Bill]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-30 |title=Abortion Legislation Bill — Third Reading - New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/combined/HansDeb_20200318_20200318_24 |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> In 2023, he stated the National Party's decision to not bloc oppose the [[Births, Deaths, Marriages, and Relationships Registration Act 2021]] and the [[Conversion Practices Prohibition Legislation Act 2022]] were part of his decision to leave the party.<ref name=":3" />

In mid-May 2019, Ngaro attracted criticism from former National MP [[Jami-Lee Ross]] and the [[Abortion Law Reform Association of New Zealand]] when he shared a [[Facebook]] post on his page likening [[abortion]] to [[the Holocaust]].<ref name="jason.walls@nzme.co.nz @Jasonwalls92">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/national-mp-alfred-ngaro-says-he-regrets-sharing-a-post-that-likened-abortion-to-the-holocaust/BNBE6RJGNV2KI7ETRFCGH3UBLA/|title=National MP Alfred Ngaro says he regrets sharing a post that likened abortion to the holocaust|last=Walls|first=Jason|newspaper=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=2019-05-20|access-date=2019-08-16|language=en-NZ|issn=1170-0777}}</ref><ref name="newstalkzb.co.nz">{{Cite 'It's not something I would say'|last=ZB|first=Newstalk|website=ZB|access-date=2019-08-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Ross |first1=Jami-Lee |title=Ngaro's support of "abortion equals Holocaust" ==Controversies==
In 2009, Alfred Ngaro allegedly punched former [[Tamaki College]] art teacher Christopher Scott Roy for not bowing his head during a prayer,<ref>{{cite news|title=Punched For Not Praying|url= http://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/9139312/Punched-for-not-praying |access-date=5 December 2013|publisher=Fairfax}}</ref> but the allegations were later dismissed in court by Chief Judge Graeme Colgan who wrote in a report: "I am sceptical about the veracity of Mr Roy's accounts of relevant and crucial events in this case. He is not a consistently reliable witness of truth."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/78045779/atheist-teacher-loses-employment-court-case-against-tamaki-college|title=Atheist teacher loses Employment Court case against Tamaki College|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en|access-date=2019-08-16}}</ref> Tamaki College denied any assault occurred. In a judgment released mid November 2013, Employment Relations Authority member Tania Tetitaha found there were several issues with Roy's statements about the alleged accusations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/business/better-business/9416034/Atheist-teacher-fails-in-ERA-bid|title=Atheist teacher fails in ERA bid|website=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |language=en|access-date=2019-08-16}}</ref> When Roy took the matter to police, they declined to investigate. The ERA also found a lack of evidence of bullying behaviour. The police and Employment Relations Authority did not investigate the incident.<ref>{{cite news|title=Atheist teacher fails in ERA bid|url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/business/better-business/9416034/Atheist-teacher-fails-in-ERA-bid|access-date=19 November 2013|publisher=Fairfax}}</ref>

In 2024, Ngaro was investigated for and cleared of assault allegations after a family funeral in the Cook Islands.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-16 |title='I did not strike her': Former Nats minister investigated over family funeral fight |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/kahu/former-national-mp-alfred-ngaro-interviewed-by-police-after-family-fight-next-to-mothers-coffin/NKW5L6D6WRH33F7GIYRBUIQNDM/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-01-16 |title=Ex-Nats MP cleared by police after family fight at mum's tangi |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/kahu/police-clear-former-national-mp-alfred-ngaro-of-assault-claims-after-family-fight-at-mums-tangi/ZZHRDCPUTBGHHL2P3ZXMT6XDH4/ |access-date=2024-01-15 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}}</ref>
